related_resources.reason: Context for Kuhn 1963 interviews and retrospective self-description of teaching quantum mechanics.
Original molecular quantum-mechanics paper motivating electronic-nuclear separation and its approximations.
Archival inquiry finds no contemporary documentary corroboration of the poisoned-apple legend; later versions contested.
Early physics career, teaching, Kitty and children, institutional leadership, AEC service and late life, with Bethe recollections.
Archival chronology and subject coverage, mostly Princeton-era papers; not a claim that every event is documented in this particular collection.
Scientist colleague and former Los Alamos theoretical-division head reflects on early physics, teaching and character; interpret retrospective appraisal accordingly.
Birth, New York family, Harvard/Cambridge/Göttingen, New Mexico, Berkeley, Tatlock, Frank, Kitty and political context. Some psychological and anecdotal details require external corroboration.
Tatlock medical education, politics, personal relationship with Oppenheimer, 1943 meeting under surveillance, and suicide in 1944; no invented motive.
Wartime organization, Groves, research community, Chevalier and Tatlock, Trinity, Japanese bombings and early postwar reactions; uses a mix of archival evidence and retrospective testimony.
Original Oppenheimer–Phillips deuteron-reaction analysis and collaboration.
Idealized gravitational collapse paper published Sep 1, 1939; later black-hole interpretations must not be backdated verbatim.
Idealized cold-neutron-gas general-relativistic equilibrium and mass limit; not accurate modern neutron-star mass bound.

description: Follows J. Robert Oppenheimer’s education and California theoretical-physics community, explaining the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, the Oppenheimer–Phillips process, relativistic neutron-star models and his work with Hartland Snyder on gravitational collapse. Connects those achievements to his political relationships and the wartime circumstances preceding Los Alamos.
